I have 12 mu and only 2 people in the household, so I will keep the farm simple and labor-efficient. I will put 10 mu into my usual wheat-maize rotation because that fits my land, my experience, and my well irrigation best. I will keep 2 mu in cotton so I still have some cash-crop income, but I will not expand cotton because it takes more labor and management. I have farmed for 30 years, so I would rather stay with a familiar structure than take extra risk at the start of the season.

For inputs, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stability, and I will keep fertilizer at moderate levels because I want steady production, not excessive cost. I will use well irrigation several times on wheat and maize because water control matters a lot in my area, and I will irrigate cotton a bit less. I will use rotary tillage for most fields because it is practical and fast for my farm size. My goal this year is stable grain output from wheat and maize, plus a smaller but manageable cotton area for income.
